ai.description: This caecilian reaches 30–40 cm. It is uniform dark brown to purplish-gray with a distinct pale stripe along the lower jaw. It is distinguished by a narrow, elongated head and 100–110 primary annuli.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis longicephalus* is best distinguished by its uniquely elongated head and a significantly higher number of primary annuli (typically >120) compared to other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis longicephalus* inhabits moist, evergreen tropical forests in the Western Ghats, typically found in damp soil near streams at elevations of 800–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Long-headed Caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis longicephalus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 20–30 eggs in moist soil near water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis longicephalus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of Kerala, India, where it inhabits moist tropical forests at elevations between 200 and 1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Ichthyophis longicephalus* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted from within subterranean tunnels or moist soil.
